description.narrative:
The Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund (AECF) is a multi-donor funded financing facility aimed at stimulating private sector driven innovations to improve market systems for enterprises in agribusinesses, renewable energy, and finance. It makes the markets work profitably better for the poor in the rural areas in Africa and stimulate further investments by private sector entrepreneurs. The Fund awards grants and non-recourse loans to projects focused on agriculture, renewable energy and adaptation to climate change, and access to financial services and information, with the aim of improving households incomes and reducing rural poverty. Based on the poverty dimensions, to achieve the goal, AECF provides catalytic financial RESOURCES as matching grants for companies, selected through a competitive process. This promotes private sector innovations and investments in projects that create OPPORTUNITIES to the poor as employees, contract farmers, out-growers and/ or suppliers.
Sida through the Embassy in Dar es Salaam bilateral strategy and the UK Department for International Development (DFID), now FCDO, has been co-funding the Agribusiness windows for rounds Two and Three (TZAW R2 & R3). The total funding about amount for Round Two (R2) has been USD 4.55 million with proportion of 76% from DFID and 24% from Sida and USD 9.15 million for Round Three (R3), with 50% from each funder. The programme had 25 projects (8 for R2 and 17 R3) representing a mix of agribusiness enterprises in Tanzania. The support agreement to TZAW R2 & R3 ended in 2020. The agreement however was shared with REACT window which was no-cost extended.
The original design of TZAW/REACT challenge funds included the repaid grants, a non-recourse loans to innovative projects focused on agriculture, renewable energy and adaptation to climate change, and access to financial services and information. However, the decision on how to use the repaid grants funds collected from the challenge fund private sector companies was not clearly decided. AECF therefore has been reaching out to donors bilaterally with proposals to reinvest the collected funds. As of December 2022, AECF reported to have collected about USD 1.7 million from Tanzania bilateral strategy window (TZAW) and in 2023 AECF reported USD 1.2 million from unspent funds from REACT min-grid challenge funds. The dialogue was done regarding the use of the funds and it was deliberated that there is potential of more development impact from having another round of challenge fund agribusiness projects and hence a no-cost extension was proposed since the repaid grant is not new funding. The decision also involved to reallocate the unspent funds from REACT to TZAW
The Seed for Impact Program (SIP), is therefore a specific window created through extension of existing AECF-TZAW window with funding from Sida, aims to transform Tanzanian's seed sector by enabling smallholder farmers to access certified, climate-resilient seed varieties. With a total investment of USD 2.9 million comprising an initial USD 1.7 million and a top-up of USD 1.2 million the program focuses on scaling the production and distribution of improved bean, sorghum, and sesame seeds. The initiative prioritizes inclusivity and sustainability by blending grant funding with private co-investment and technical assistance, particularly targeting underserved regions such as Mbeya, Songwe, Kilimanjaro, Katavi, Manyara, Dodoma, and Ruvuma. The objective is to invest in measurable and demonstrable impact at the local scale, to build a lasting impact for the expansion of the approach to other regions in future.

AECF-Agribusiness Window for Tanzania is a challenge fund that aims to co-finance and stimulate, innovative and catalytic private agri-business investments in Tanzania. It is implemented by AGRA (Alliance for Green Revloution in Africa).

Tilläggsbeslutet gäller ett tillskott till AECF för att finansiera en tredje runda av Tanzania Agri-business Window (TZAW) där företag kan söka stöd för affärsmodeller inom jordbrukssektorn som gynnar människor som lever i fattigdom. Ett antal vinnande företag väljs ut bland annat baserat på hur väl och hur många fattiga människor kan dra nytta av företagets affärsmodell, som producenter, konsumenter, leverantörer mm.
Tidigare stöd har gått till runda två av TZAW och Renewable Energy and Climate Change Adaptation Technologies (REACT-TZ). Det är ännu för tidigt att rapportera resultat från dessa två utlysningar, men rapportering från första rundan (ej finansierad av Sida-stöd) visar resultat i linje med uppsatta målsättningar och visar att modellen fungerar väl.
Det bedöms finnas ett ansenligt antal lovande företag inom jordbrukssektorn i Tanzania som skulle kunna kvalificera för AECF-stöd. Utifrån goda förutsättningar och baserat på erfarenheter av redan pågående verksamhet genom AECF i Tanzania bedöms ett stöd till en tredje runda av TZAW vara relevant. Den tredje rundan kommer att innebära en väsentlig ökning av det förväntade antalet människor som ska öka sina inkomster som en följd av projekten.

description.narrative:
The first year of implementing the new Seed for Impact Programme challenge funds mainly involved the process of running the challenge funds competition, due-diligence and commissioning of the projects. The first round processes are reported to be complete.
During the first year AECF undertook scoping study on the status of climate resilient crop varieties and access to germplasm by the private seed enterprises in Tanzania. The research was conducted to gain an understanding of the status of climate-resilient crop varieties in Tanzania and recommend specific crop varieties to be promoted, along with strategies for scaling up adoption. It focused on specific questions related to the national catalogue of crop varieties, engagement with stakeholders in crop improvement, organizations involved in improving climate-resilient crop varieties, the role of research organizations in creating awareness of improved and climate-resilient crop varieties, and the status of plant breeders' rights in Tanzania.
The second activity was running the challenge fund competition, due diligence and commissioning of projects. The process involved a call for competition publicized on the AECF website and other media outlets as well as workshops, and proposal submissions through the official submittable platform and proposal review by a competent team of experts. Ten proposal were received. After successfully passing the proposal stage, companies underwent comprehensive business planning and due diligence phases. Three companies Agrinature, Namburi and Kinemo, were approved for funding and contracting was finalized in March 2024.
Regarding the challenge funds financing outcome, the report shows that the approved grant funding to Agrinature Company Limited to the tune of US$ 499,680 with matching funds of US$ 203,532, for a project valued at US$ 703,248. For Kinemo Agro Seeds and Chemicals Traders Co. Ltd to the approved funding is around US$ 178,187.10 with matching funds of US$ 67,194.90, for the project valued at US$ 245,382. Upon contracting the above approved companies for funding, an initial US$ 158, 196.00 were disbursed to enable them to start the project activities. Moreover reports shows the disbursement schedule and the goal is to ensure 90% of the investment funds goes out by end of the year 2024 and the developmemt results are expected to be reported in the 2025 reporting.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
